label: Semi-skimmed milk
note: In the US and UK, "low-fat milk" means about 1 % fat, lower than semi-skimmed (about 1.5–2 %). The US counterpart of semi-skimmed is reduced-fat milk at 2 %.

about.text: Milk with part of its fat taken out: in the EU it must have between 1.5 and 1.8 % fat, against at least 3.5 % for whole milk and no more than 0.5 % for skimmed.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: Cream fat is measured by flow and by density, and the two are combined for a fast, accurate correction; the result repeats within 0.015 % fat (sd)
The cream to be homogenised should be at most 18 % fat; it is mixed with surplus skim milk (to e.g. 3 % fat) after homogenisation
